claims.sentence: To request accommodations for ongoing and interim assessments, you must submit a written application
You must also submit a written request to receive additional time to prepare your answer during a test or an exam
The university will develop adapted evaluation materials for your assessment
These materials must make it possible to evaluate the achievement of learning outcomes and the level of all competences’ development mentioned in your education program
The form of your assessment will be defined taking into account the peculiarities of your mental and physical development
The available forms include verbal responses, written responses on paper and computer, and tests
If you have a serious health problem such as a speech disorder, deafness, or hard of hearing, oral assessments must be held in written form
If you have a visual impairment, the university must provide an assistant to provide you with the necessary assistance during pass fail exam and exams
Written exercises will be dictated to an assistant
A technical assistive device will be provided for task completion in case of necessity, and the usage of your own technical assistive devices is also possible
You might use assistive devices during the assessment sessions taking into consideration your special needs
You are entitled to additional time to prepare your answer during a test or an exam
The duration of an assessment session cannot be extended to more than 1.5 hours
The evidence does not specify the deadline for submitting the written application or written request
The evidence does not state which office or staff member processes these requests or where they should be submitted
The evidence does not define the exact procedures for developing the adapted evaluation materials or how the assessment form is officially selected
The evidence does not specify how the additional time is calculated or what happens if the 1.5-hour limit is reached
The evidence does not cover accommodations for disabilities or health conditions other than visual impairment, speech disorders, deafness, or hard of hearing
The evidence does not address interim assessments for students without disabilities or serious health conditions
Individual course pages may provide additional details or differ from these regulations, but the official document takes precedence
